prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1046; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Please tell me in your own words what happened on the day of the accident.

A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in Baytown, waiting to turn. The car behind me didn't stop in time and hit me from the back. It wasn't a huge impact, but I felt it right away.

Q: Were you able to get out of your vehicle at the scene?

A: Yes, I got out and walked around. The other driver said they were sorry and looked shaken up. We exchanged information and waited for the police to come.

Q: Did you go to a doctor or an urgent care afterward?

A: I went to urgent care that same evening. They checked my neck and back and said I had a neck strain. They gave me a prescription for a muscle relaxer and told me to rest and use ice.

Q: Are you still having symptoms?

A: Yes. My neck is stiff, especially when I turn my head to check traffic or back out of the driveway. Some mornings the pain is worse, and I get a dull ache between my shoulders.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: I took a few days off to rest, and I've been limiting how long I sit at my desk. I'm working, but it's been uncomfortable.

Q: Do you currently have a follow-up appointment scheduled?

A: Yes, I have a visit with my primary care doctor next week. They're going to decide whether I need physical therapy.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you think I should know about the accident or your injuries?

A: No, I think that covers it. I'll send over the urgent care paperwork when I get home.

Q: Thank you for your time. We'll be in touch soon.
